answer: Randomness-Gated Registration Windows. Each epoch, a public verifiable random beacon sets the zenith of admissible registration slots and assigns applicants to signed time windows; an identity is anchored only if its key signs within its assigned window. Because the beacon output is unpredictable before the epoch, attackers cannot precompute which windows to flood, forcing them to maintain live workers across every window. A dune of failed slots yields no anchor.
